methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 11 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Ranovus is a Series D+ semiconductor company founded by Hamid Arabzadeh that has raised $236M in total capital, including a $36M strategic investment fund grant in August 2025. The valuation universe comprises 11 private peers in Chips & Semiconductors alongside three public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD), though the private peer set includes only 8 investable private companies, with Cerebras, SambaNova Systems, PsiQuantum, Etched, and Tenstorrent representing the most proximate competitors.

The peer-median method proved inapplicable to this analysis. Despite the existence of 11 same-sector peers, zero companies met the filtering criteria for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier comparability. A fallback to all-sector median multiples would introduce unacceptable bias given stage heterogeneity and capital intensity variance across the semiconductor landscape. This constraint reflects the sparse, high-variance nature of late-stage private semiconductor financing.

Without a sufficiently dense comparable set meeting stage and tier specificity requirements, triangulation via peer multiples cannot be reliably executed. Any valuation range derived from this dataset would rest on either (1) public semiconductor multiples applied to private-company fundamentals—a methodologically weak substitution given public company scale and profitability—or (2) single-point reference pricing from the top five named private peers, both approaches carrying material uncertainty. A credible valuation would require either additional same-stage private transactions or forward-looking DCF anchored to capital intensity benchmarks and time-to-revenue visibility.
